content.title: Houston basketball March Madness: Cougars roll past Idaho in opener
content.text: OKLAHOMA CITY — Before Thursday’s NCAA Tournament first-round game against Idaho, Kelvin Sampson could sense some nervousness from freshmen Kingston Flemings and Chris Cenac Jr. As Sampson put it, Flemings and Cenac were acting “freshmany.” “They’ve never been here before,” Sampson said during an in-game interview with truTV. “You could tell they were a little nervous. Emanuel is not nervous.” After a slow start, second-seeded Houston cruised to a 78-47 win over 15-seed Idaho before a crowd of 13,815 at Paycom Center, setting up a second-round matchup with Texas A&M at 5:10 p.m. Saturday. UH (29-6) took its first step and is one win away from a seventh straight trip to the Sweet 16, which will be held at Toyota Center. After trailing Idaho 12-9 in the opening five minutes, UH went on a 24-3 run. Emanuel Sharp hit three 3-pointers and scored 10 points during the stretch as the Cougars went ahead 33-15. Idaho (21-15), the Big Sky tournament champion, went more than six minutes without a field goal. In their NCAA Tournament debuts, Flemings had a game-high 18 points, six rebounds four assists and Cenac added seven points and a career-high 17 rebounds. Joseph Tugler added 13 points, including a poster dunk off an assist from Sharp in the second half. Sharp finished with 16 points on 6-of-7 shooting. Kolton Mitchell had 14 points for Idaho, which shot 28.6% for the game. — Joseph Duarte Key content •  How two freshman played like veterans for Cougars •  Emanuel Sharp's big shots, and message•  A dose of 'Bucky Ball' for Texas A&M•  How to watch UH vs. Texas A&M•  Texas Longhorns looking like a dangerous team Here’s how the game played out: Coogs on cruise control UH has opened up a 30-point lead with less than five minutes left. It’s looking very much like the second NCAA Tournament matchup with Texas A&M in three seasons coming Saturday. — Greg Rajan Attendance report The announced attendance for the late session here at Paycom Center is 13,815. The afternoon session was even rowdier with Nebraska seemingly filling the building on its own as the Huskers won their first tournament game in program history. There’s going to be a lot of red in this building Saturday with the Huskers fans back to watch their team play Vanderbilt as the nightcap to the Houston-Texas A&M meeting. — Matt Young Kingston Flemings, one cool customer Houston freshman point guard Kingston Flemings will get a stiffer test against the Texas A&M defense Saturday, but he appears unfazed by his first NCAA tournament appearance. With the Cougars leading 59-33 with 11:13 remaining, the best freshman basketball player in program history has an efficient 14 points on 6-of-8 shooting to go along with six rebounds and four assists. — Matt Young Tugler throws one down JoJo Tugler just delivered a poster dunk with about 13 minutes left in the game. On a fast break, Emanuel Sharp lost the handle on the ball and flipped to Tugler coming down the middle. Idaho’s Kolton Mitchell could only get out of the way. — Joseph Duarte Chase McCarty back in Chase McCarty, who left the game after taking a hard fall during the first half, checks back into the game for UH. — Joseph Duarte Looking ahead Assuming UH holds this commanding lead, the Cougars would play at 5:10 p.m. CT on Saturday against Texas A&M. The game will be broadcast on TNT. — Greg Rajan Halftime: UH 48, Idaho 24 It’s been all Cougars for the first 20 minutes. Kingston Flemings has a game-high 14 points (6-of-6 shooting), Emanuel Sharp has 12 (three 3s) and Chris Cenac Jr. has 12 rebounds. UH shot 60% from the field while Idaho struggled at 27%. The Cougars pulled away with a 24-3 run and later added an 11-0 run. “We started getting stops on defense. That’s really where it all started,” Sharp said in a halftime interview with Andy Katz. — Joseph Duarte Chris Cenac Jr. controlling the boards Chris Cenac Jr. has 12 rebounds in the first half, two shy of his career high. Cenac has played with a high motor after having a little chat with Kelvin Sampson a few minutes earlier. — Joseph Duarte Nervous? Not Kingston Flemings About those NCAA Tournament jitters… Houston freshman Kingston Flemings, who was named consensus second-team All-American, has a game-high 14 points on a perfect 6-of-6 shooting. — Joseph Duarte Idaho struggling from distance Idaho led the Big Sky with 337 3-pointers this season but has struggled from beyond the arc in the first half. The Vandals are just 3-of-14 from 3-point range. — Joseph Duarte UH out to biggest lead The Cougars are up 42-20 with 3:47 left in the first half after a Chris Cenac Jr. 3-pointer. — Greg Rajan Vandals' drought ends Idaho went more than six minutes between field goals until Kolton Mitchell’s jumper with 5:50 left in the first half. — Joseph Duarte McCarty shaken up UH’s Chase McCarty is dealing with a leg injury after taking a hard fall to the floor while trying to block a shot with 6:55 left in the first half. — Greg Rajan 7:24 left in first half It’s 33-15 UH, which is in the midst of a 24-3 run. Idaho is shooting 31.6% (6 for 19) to UH’s 55% (11 for 20). The Cougars are 4 of 6 from 3-point range. — Greg Rajan Praise for Emanuel Sharp In an interview with sideline reporter Andy Katz, Kelvin Sampson credited Emanuel Sharp’s leadership to calm down freshmen Kingston Flemings and Chris Cenac Jr., who he said were “freshmany.” “They’ve never been here before. You could tell they were a little nervous, Emanuel is not nervous.” — Joseph Duarte Familiar leaders for UH Kingston Flemings and Emanuel Sharp have been the Cougars' top scorers all season and it’s no different in the first half Thursday. The All-Big 12 guards are a combined 7-of-8 for 20 points. — Joseph Duarte Coogs taking over After a slow start, the Cougars have turned it on as we reach the halfway mark of the first half. UH went on a 12-0 run, highlighted by 10 points by Emanuel Sharp, to take a 25-15 lead. Since the Vandals went ahead 12-9, UH has outscored Idaho 16-3. — Joseph Duarte Sharp shooter Emanuel Sharp, who has struggled offensively in recent games, is off to a hot start with seven consecutive points for Houston. Sharp was fouled on a 3-pointer for a four-point play, and added another 3 on the next trip down the floor, extending his school record to 303 career 3s. Sharp’s run put the Cougars ahead 16-12. — Joseph Duarte Close game early Thanks to a couple of early 3-pointers, Idaho holds a 10-7 lead a little more than four minutes into the game. The Vandals have made 4 of 8 shots to 2 of 7 for the Cougars. — Greg Rajan Big 12's campaign for UH as a No. 1 Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark said the league sent the NCAA selection committee “a lot of data” to campaign for Houston to be a No. 1 region seed in the NCAA Tournament. Florida ended up getting the final No. 1 seed in the South Region. UH’s consolation prize was the chance to play the second weekend of the tournament at Toyota Center. “On behalf on the conference, we put a lot of data in front of the selection committee,” Yormark said. “We thought they had a better résumé than Florida. But it worked out  just fine for Houston.” — Joseph Duarte Big 12 all about UH playing close to home After a tough draw last year, Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark says Houston has “turned the tables” with the chance to play the second weekend of the NCAA Tournament at Toyota Center. “I spent a lot of time with Kelvin (Sampson) last year and those were home games for Tennessee and specifically for Purdue,” Yormark said of last year’s Midwest Region held in Indianapolis. “We’ve turned the table this year. They get past this weekend and obviously they are going home. That means a lot for Houston and the conference. So, we’re excited about the possibility.” The South Region (Sweet 16 and Elite Eight rounds) is scheduled for next Thursday and Saturday. — Joseph Duarte Same starting five for UH It’s the same starting five for Houston: Kingston Flemings, Milos Uzan, Emanuel Sharp, Chris Cenac Jr. and Joseph Tugler.  — Joseph Duarte Texas A&M wins, awaits the winner of UH-Idaho The 10th-seeded Aggies had no problem with Saint Mary’s in a 63-50 win and will play the winner of Houston-Idaho on Saturday for the right to go to the Sweet 16 at Toyota Center. — Matt Young Who would Houston play next? Houston is a 24-point favorite over Idaho tonight, so it’s not absurd to look ahead to who the Cougars would face Saturday with a win. Right now, it’s looking like it will be Texas A&M. The 10-seed Aggies overwhelmed 7-seed Saint Mary’s (Calif.) in the first half. Texas A&M leads 37-26 at halftime and its trademark Bucky Ball after head coach Bucky McMillan is showing up, forcing 11 turnovers in the game’s opening 20 minutes. — Matt Young Pregame reading •  How Kingston Flemings became UH’s best freshman basketball player ever•  'The JoJo Rules.' 'They’ve earned the right.' How to watch, stream and listen When: 9:10 p.m. ThursdayTV: truTV with Brandon Gaudin (play-by-play), Chris Webber (analyst) and Andy Katz (sideline reporter).Streaming: On the March Madness Live App (must authenticate using TV provider) or on HBO Max (for all TBS, TNT and truTV games, subscription required) Radio:  950 AM with Jeremy Branham (play-by-play) and Elvin Hayes (analyst).
